conventions.convention: The integral uses a continuous complex amplitude, continuous real phase, a<b, and nonzero real frequency. Complex Riemann integrals are defined componentwise; C^r on a closed interval uses one-sided endpoint derivatives.
Nonstationarity requires |g'|≥c>0 on the entire interval of application. T_g^0h=h and T_g^(j+1)h=(T_g^jh/g')'.
Fourier moments start at degree zero, permit m=0, and use exact real and complex arithmetic.
Levin collocation includes both endpoints, uses L_ωp=p'+iωg'p, returns failure for singular A, and otherwise solves in exact arithmetic. Matrix norms are induced Euclidean norms.
The damped Gaussian uses the continuous square-root branch on Re α>0 with arg α∈(-π/2,π/2). The whole-line Fresnel integral is an ordinary improper integral with separately convergent tails.
Filon nodes include a and b; moment estimates carry individual absolute errors ε_j, with total moment budget η_n=Σ|f(c_j)|ε_j.

The stationary-phase branch requires exactly one simple interior critical point and no other zero of g' on the closed interval. Its Fresnel sign is sgn(ωg''(x_0)); complementary T_g derivatives are extended by zero where the complementary amplitude vanishes near x_0.

The approximate Levin solve residual is the exact algebraic residual ρ=Aĉ-y. Its bound includes both the continuous collocation error and inverse-matrix amplification; it does not certify a rounded residual.

load_bearing.statement: For a<b, integer r≥1, nonzero real ω, real g∈C^(r+1)[a,b] with |g'|≥c>0, and complex h∈C^r[a,b], I_ω(h,g)=Σ_(j=0)^(r-1) (-1)^j(iω)^(-j-1)[(T_g^jh/g')e^(iωg)]_a^b+(-1)^r(iω)^(-r)I_ω(T_g^rh,g). The remainder modulus is at most (b-a)|ω|^(-r)||T_g^rh||∞.

For Re α>0, the absolutely convergent componentwise integral F(α)=∫_ℝ exp(-αu²)du equals √π α^(-1/2) on the specified continuous branch. For every λ>0 and σ∈{-1,1}, the ordinary two-sided improper integral ∫_ℝ exp(iσλu²/2)du equals √(2π/λ)exp(iσπ/4).

For real g∈C^7(J) on an open interval and x_0∈J with g'(x_0)=0 and g''(x_0)≠0, some neighborhood admits an increasing C^5 diffeomorphism Φ satisfying g(x)=g(x_0)+sgn(g''(x_0))Φ(x)²/2, Φ(x_0)=0, and Φ'(x_0)=√|g''(x_0)|.

For R>0, λ≥1, σ∈{-1,1}, A∈C_c^4((-R,R);ℂ), and a fixed even smooth compactly supported cutoff χ equal to one near zero, the difference between ∫_(-R)^R A(u)exp(iσλu²/2)du and A(0)√(2π/λ)exp(iσπ/4) has modulus at most C_(R,χ)||A||_(C^4)λ^(-3/2).

For n≥1, distinct real nodes c_0,…,c_n, and arbitrary complex values y_0,…,y_n, p=Σy_jℓ_j is the unique polynomial of degree at most n with p(c_j)=y_j; interpolation reproduces every polynomial of degree at most n.

Under its stated nonstationary smoothness and nonsingular collocation hypotheses, I_ω(f,g)-Q=I_ω(f-L_ωp,g), with the stated repeated integration-by-parts expansion and E_j,V_j,K_s bound. For exact algebraic residual ρ=Aĉ-y, |Q(ĉ)-Q|≤||d||₂||A^(-1)||₂||ρ||₂; adding this to B_s bounds the total integral error.
